name: Phishing & malicious attachment response
description: Contain a user who opened a phishing lure and purge the campaign.
steps: Pull the original email (headers, sender, URLs, attachment hash) from the mail gateway.
Search and purge the same message from all mailboxes.
Block sender domain, URLs and attachment hash at the gateway and proxy.
Check whether the attachment executed on the endpoint (process tree, EDR).
If executed: isolate the host and reset the user's credentials.
Notify the user and run targeted awareness follow-up.

name: Malicious execution & credential theft
description: Respond to PowerShell/LOLBin execution and credential dumping on an endpoint.
steps: Isolate the endpoint via EDR (keep it powered on).
Capture memory and triage disk image for forensics.
Decode any encoded commands and extract further IOCs.
Reset passwords for every account logged on to the host; revoke Kerberos tickets/sessions.
Hunt for the same hashes and command lines across the fleet.
Rebuild the host from a known-good image.

name: Brute force & account compromise
description: Handle password guessing followed by a successful login.
steps: Block the attacking source IPs at the perimeter.
Determine whether any login succeeded after the failures.
If yes: disable/reset the account, kill active sessions, review commands executed.
Check for persistence (cron, authorized_keys, new users, services).
Enforce key-based SSH / MFA and lockout policy.

name: Web application exploitation
description: Respond to SQL injection, Log4Shell and other attacks on public-facing apps.
steps: Block the attacking IPs at the WAF and add virtual-patch rules.
Check application and outbound logs for successful exploitation (callbacks, new files, errors).
Patch the vulnerable component (e.g. Log4j >= 2.17.1) - cross-check the VA findings for this asset.
Search for web shells and unexpected child processes of the web server.
Rotate application secrets if compromise is confirmed.

name: Lateral movement containment
description: Stop an attacker moving between internal hosts.
steps: Identify source and destination hosts and the account used.
Isolate both hosts; disable the account used for movement.
Block RDP/SMB between workstation segments.
Review the destination host for persistence and data staging.
Patch exploitable remote services (MS17-010, RDP without NLA).

name: C2 beaconing & data exfiltration
description: Cut attacker command-and-control and scope data loss.
steps: Block C2 IPs/domains at firewall, proxy and DNS.
Find every internal host that contacted the C2 infrastructure.
Isolate beaconing hosts and collect forensics.
Quantify data transferred (flow logs, proxy bytes out) and identify the data.
Engage legal/privacy for breach assessment if personal data was involved.

name: Ransomware response
description: Contain ransomware and protect recovery capability.
steps: Isolate affected hosts immediately; disconnect shared drives.
Disable compromised accounts and block ransomware IOCs fleet-wide.
Protect and verify offline backups before restoring.
Identify the initial access vector and patient zero.
Activate the incident response plan: management, legal, regulators as required.
Restore from clean backups and monitor for re-infection.

name: Privileged group / account manipulation
description: Investigate unexpected changes to privileged groups or accounts.
steps: Confirm whether a change ticket authorises the change.
If not: remove the membership and disable the actor account.
Review the actor's recent logons and the DC security log.
Check domain controllers for exploitation (e.g. PrintNightmare) and persistence.
Rotate KRBTGT and privileged credentials if domain compromise is suspected.
